# Retrospective

## Worked

Read-only security triage preceded both reviewer launches and all PR runtime work. Managed Herdr context and Team 4 ownership were checked first. Both technical reviewers received equivalent neutral scope in fresh verified sessions; neither report was opened until both finals existed. Source-only Sol and coordinator inspections independently supported the upgrade-path concern. No desktop slots, real accounts, system mutations or upstream posting were used. The final comment avoids unsupported test totals and keeps the conditional package premise explicit.

## Avoidable friction and remediation

Opus's first main fixture produced symlinks that the evidence sealer rejects. It remains preserved and excluded; v2 recorded links before removing only its own links. This is a known tool boundary, not a demonstrated new tool bug.

More importantly, the retention-adapted stock test still lacked per-final-target assertions in its own setup/stubs. Several substitution/pipeline producers were unchecked and rerun logs mixed phases. A parent-root check and valid seal were insufficient. Coordinator inspected the actual fixture, withdrew stock/rerun coverage from public claims, requested an audit addendum and received explicit acceptance with safety_process_compliant=false. No rerun was necessary because source evidence resolved the material public questions. Preserve both raw runs and independent final rather than silently rewriting history.

Assignment-local correction for future reuse: before invoking a stock test, compare its entire literal target/producer checklist with the actual adapted test and every generated stub. If any write, redirection, status, substitution or phase snapshot lacks its own gate, do not claim full guard coverage or broad behavioral totals. Either use a fully audited adaptation or state source-only scope. The same correction was sent directly to the responsible reviewer in this assignment. No persistent agent memory was edited.

Initial policy-read truncation was corrected before Opus runtime. Sol's failed initial discussion parser was corrected before use. Harness-help discovery and assignment-local Git materialization are orchestration/source preparation, not PR runtime tests. Automatic native histories remain under managed session storage.

## Carry forward

Separate a useful immediate repair from ongoing package lifecycle coverage. Treat current AUR packaging as a proxy and label it, not as proof of exact Omarchy or future artifacts. Preserve administrator-owned local paths during optional alias setup. Keep convention-only and uncommon edge-case notes local when they would dilute the main review. No additional tooling/Omadev issue was established.
comment:
Two issues remain in the repair path at `3d976934ba27`: package upgrades can undo it, and the migration can replace a locally managed command.

### Keep the repair effective after package upgrades

The helper runs after the explicit service installer and through a one-time migration. Later updates install packages again, but the completed migration is skipped. If the `1password` package still ships the policy and MCP permissions reported in #11830 and #12030, replacing those files restores the incorrect state.

Source-inspected sequence, not an executed package upgrade:

```text
First update:  package files -> repair owners/group/mode -> migration marked done
Later update: package files -> completed migration skipped -> repair not reapplied
```

**Impact:** The build-host polkit owner and missing MCP setgid can return after a subsequent 1Password upgrade. The current AUR install script reapplies BrowserSupport permissions on upgrade, but does not repair the MCP binary or policy; the exact Omarchy package artifact was not inspected.

**Suggested change:** Apply the repair in the package's install/upgrade hooks, or through a narrowly scoped post-transaction hook, retaining the migration for existing installations. A separately corrected package would also resolve this concern.

### Preserve an existing local MCP command

The helper [unconditionally uses `ln -sfn`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/3d976934ba2796540a1c1bbbf928f888e2ac0456/bin/omarchy-1password-finish-install#L82-L84) for `/usr/local/bin/1password-mcp` when that directory exists. This runs during migration as well as explicit installation.

```text
Existing local executable or unrelated symlink
  -> ln -sfn
  -> replaced with the packaged MCP helper link
```

**Impact:** An administrator-managed wrapper or alternate installation at that path is silently replaced. This is a conditional collision identified from source, not an observed change to a live system.

**Suggested change:** Create the convenience link only when the path is absent or already points to the intended helper. Preserve other entries and report the conflict.

**Verified (source inspection):** The service installer places the repair after package installation and before launching 1Password. The helper covers both existing owner annotations and unresolved owner templates, and applies the helper group before requesting setgid.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Pinned source, linked issue reports and current AUR packaging inspection. Runtime test results are not relied on for these findings. No real package upgrade, polkit authorization or MCP authentication was tested.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra Medium performed initial inspection and synthesis, with independent technical assessments by Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh. Final claims were checked against source and packaging evidence; a fresh Astra Medium check assessed presentation and privacy.
